David — thanks for the note and for attaching your procurement packet. High-level answers up front:

- Default retention: for Redwood Hosted, debug/operational logs (request/response traces and aggregated telemetry) are retained for 72 hours by default; ephemeral KV-cache data used for live sessions is not persisted beyond the session unless the customer explicitly enables longer retention.
- Training: Redwood does NOT use customer prompt/response content to update model weights by default. Any use of customer data for model training requires an explicit contractual opt-in and a documented export process.
- Opt-out mechanism: we expose a tenancy-level training_exclusion flag and per-request headers (x-redwood-no-train) that mark data as ineligible for downstream training pipelines. The exclusion metadata is stored with the tenancy configuration and honored by ingestion and offline training pipelines.
- Redaction/filtering: we apply redaction-on-ingest for common PII patterns (SSNs, credit cards, long sequences that look like PHI) and offer a post-processing export filter that removes or tokenizes fields customers tag as sensitive. Customers can also provide custom regex rules for their tenancy.

I've attached a short excerpt from our SIG package and a one-page playbook draft; Priyom will follow up with the sanitized CSV sample. If you prefer, we can convert the playbook into a one-page slide for procurement.

Next steps: Priyom will send the filtered logs sample and an operational snippet showing the no-train header example. Soojin can add the security controls section if you want more detail on redaction rules.

Naomi Feldman
Director, Solutions Security
Redwood Inference

Thanks Naomi — draft attached. Key operational points I included in the playbook (short form):

- Environment defaults: Hosted = 72-hour operational logs; Dedicated = configurable (0–365 days) under customer contract; Private = customer-managed retention that follows their on-prem policy.
- Training exclusion: the tenancy-level training_exclusion flag + per-request header (x-redwood-no-train) are enforced at ingest. We also persist an immutable audit record (timestamp, request id, tenancy id) that the data was excluded.
- Export/redaction workflow: exports run through the export-filter service which applies: (a) pattern redaction (SSN/CCN/Email), (b) configurable field masking, (c) optional tokenization for long-form responses. We include a sample filtered-logs-sample.csv showing header columns we export (timestamp, request_id, route, model_variant, prompt_tokens_count, response_tokens_count, redaction_status).
- Training and legal: no automated retrain on customer data without an executed training agreement. If a customer signs a training agreement, data ingress goes through a quarantine and review pipeline; customers can scope which datasets are permitted.

Operational note for the SIG Qs: provide concrete copies of the export-filter rules is out of scope for public docs, but we can provide a sanitized rule-set under NDA.

- Soojin: add the controls references (SOC 2 map).
- Karthik: attach the example header showing the x-redwood-no-train usage in curl.
